work.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave

passageLocation.openingWords: From that moment, I understood the pathway

text: From that moment, I understood the pathway from slavery to freedom. It was just what I wanted, and I got it at a time when I the least expected it. Whilst I was saddened by the thought of losing the aid of my kind mistress, I was gladdened by the invaluable instruction which, by the merest accident, I had gained from my master. Though conscious of the difficulty of learning without a teacher, I set out with high hope, and a fixed purpose, at whatever cost of trouble, to learn how to read.

assessments.conclusion: The underlying English text is outside the usual copyright term: Douglass died in 1895 and UK written works usually remain protected for 70 years after the author's death.
Project Gutenberg identifies this 1845 English text transcription as public domain in the USA.

rights.caveat: This record covers Douglass's clean English text in the intended initial GB and US markets. Its historical language and account of enslavement must retain accurate authorship and context.

curation.rationale: Douglass joins reading with freedom through language of revelation, accident, hope, purpose and difficulty. The extract preserves his historical argument while offering strong paths around learning and resolve.
